clock_plan.note: Qwen ROM die generator (tools/qwen_rom_fulldie.py SPINE_BLOCKS / IO_BLOCKS): constants_sequencer stream_1p2 (1.2 GHz), io collective (ot_rom_oneshot_die_m) serial_0p9 (0.9 GHz), vector_memory serial_0p9. The first native-coll bench assumed the opposite (sequencer 0.9 / engine 1.2); the die plan row is eng0p9_seq1p2.
clock_plan.reference_row: eng1p2_seq1p2 (single 1.2 GHz clock = the measured token-path AR windows)

token_path.note: the measured AR windows (1,094 / 949 cycles, single 1.2 GHz clock RTL) are kept; the production die runs the collective engine at 0.9 GHz: +144 cycles per 256-word all-reduce (transport only, bench-measured). NOT yet included: the 0.9 GHz vector-memory read/write share of each AR window (not re-measured).

levers.engine_at_1p2: move ot_rom_oneshot_die_m to stream_1p2 (CDC at the SerDes face instead): recovers all 144 cycles/AR (eng1p2_seq1p2 row); blocked by qfd_io_collective not closing even at its current plan (TT -340.7, live struct jobs)
levers.wider_return: two return channels / 2-word return: no gain at 256 words (the engine word rate, not the return path, bounds the AR; eng0p9 rows equal with any sequencer clock)
levers.sequencer_side_1p2: already 1.2 GHz in the die plan; the 0.9 GHz-sequencer row (eng1p2_seq0p9) costs +45/AR vs reference
levers.overlap: stream the all-reduce out of the o_proj / down matvec as words are produced: up to min(op, AR) per AR hidden; a sequencer program-structure change (segment END barrier), not benched
